chunks.text:
1. Customer Acceptance Policy
Verify that the board-approved customer acceptance policy is documented,
available to all branches, and consistent with the latest RBI master
direction on KYC.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
2. CDD Verification Sample
Select a sample of at least thirty accounts opened in the quarter and
verify that customer identity was verified using an officially valid
document and that the verification was recorded in the system.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
3. Risk Classification Coverage
Verify that every account carries a risk classification (low, medium or
high) and that enhanced due diligence was applied for high risk accounts
and politically exposed persons.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
4. KYC Updation Compliance
Verify that KYC updation was performed within the prescribed frequency for
each risk category and that accounts with pending updation were flagged.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
5. Record Retention Checks
Verify that customer identification records and transaction records are
retained for the prescribed period and that the retention register is
maintained and signed by the branch manager.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
6. Staff Training Records
Verify that all staff handling customer onboarding have completed the
mandatory KYC and anti-money laundering training in the current year and
that training records are available for inspection.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
7. Escalation and Exception Log
Verify that exceptions, deferrals and escalations in the KYC process are
logged with reasons and that the compliance team reviewed the exception
log in the current quarter.
chunks.title: KYC Audit Checklist for Internal Audit Teams

chunks.text:
1. Customer Onboarding Procedure
Branch staff shall complete customer identity verification at the time of
account opening using the bank's approved document verification application.
A photocopy or electronic image of the verifying document shall be captured
and stored in the customer record. Onboarding shall be rejected when the
verification document cannot be authenticated.
chunks.title: Internal Policy - KYC Implementation Guidelines for Branch Staff

chunks.text:
2. Verification Steps for Walk-in Customers
For walk-in customers, staff shall check the identity document against the
central KYC database, confirm the photograph matches the applicant, and
record the customer's risk classification in the onboarding system before
activating the account.
chunks.title: Internal Policy - KYC Implementation Guidelines for Branch Staff

chunks.text:
3. Document Requirements for High Risk Accounts
Accounts classified as high risk shall require two identity documents and
a proof of address, together with a declaration of the source of funds.
The branch manager shall approve such accounts before activation.
chunks.title: Internal Policy - KYC Implementation Guidelines for Branch Staff

chunks.text:
4. Handling Requests for KYC Updation
When a customer approaches for KYC updation, staff shall verify the
documents afresh, update the risk classification if warranted, and record
the updation in the system with the date and time. Customers shall be
informed of the outcome within five working days.
chunks.title: Internal Policy - KYC Implementation Guidelines for Branch Staff

chunks.text:
5. Escalation for Unverified Records
Where KYC records are pending updation for more than the regulatory
timeline, staff shall flag the account in the system and seek approval
from the compliance team before restricting account operations. The
customer shall be informed before any restriction is applied.
chunks.title: Internal Policy - KYC Implementation Guidelines for Branch Staff

chunks.text:
1. Disclosure of Charges
Banks shall display a complete schedule of service charges and fees on
their website and at every branch in a customer-friendly format. The
schedule shall list each charge, the basis on which the charge is levied,
and the frequency of levying the charge.
chunks.title: Disclosure of Charges and Fees for Banking Services

chunks.text:
1.1 Prior Notice of Revision
No bank shall revise or introduce any charge or fee without giving the
customer prior notice of at least thirty days before the effective date.
The notice shall be sent through SMS, email or letter and shall clearly
state the existing charge and the revised charge.
chunks.title: Disclosure of Charges and Fees for Banking Services

chunks.text:
1.2 Customer Consent
Banks shall obtain explicit consent from the customer before levying any
new charge on an existing product or service. In the absence of such
consent, the bank shall provide the customer the option to close the
account or switch to an alternate product without penalty.
chunks.title: Disclosure of Charges and Fees for Banking Services

chunks.text:
1.3 Penal Charges on Loans
Penal interest or penal charges on loans shall be based on the outstanding
amount for which default occurred and shall not be a means of revenue
enhancement. Excessive penal charges that are not proportionate to the
delayed amount shall be treated as usury.
chunks.title: Disclosure of Charges and Fees for Banking Services

chunks.text:
1.4 Communication of Changes
Whenever a bank revises its schedule of charges, it shall update the
website and mobile application within seven days of the effective date and
shall communicate a summary of changes to customers along with the monthly
statement or by other electronic means.
chunks.title: Disclosure of Charges and Fees for Banking Services

chunks.text:
1. Internal Grievance Redressal
Every bank shall have a dedicated internal grievance redressal mechanism
and shall designate a nodal officer to acknowledge and resolve customer
complaints. Complaints may be lodged through the branch, the call centre,
the website or the mobile application.
chunks.title: Customer Grievance Redressal Framework

chunks.text:
1.1 Acknowledgement and Resolution Timelines
Banks shall acknowledge every complaint within three working days of
receipt. The bank shall resolve the complaint and communicate the decision
to the customer within thirty days from the date of receipt of the
complaint. If additional information is required, the timeline shall be
recomputed from the date of receipt of such information.
chunks.title: Customer Grievance Redressal Framework

chunks.text:
1.2 Escalation to Internal Ombudsman
If the customer is not satisfied with the bank's response, the customer may
approach the Internal Ombudsman of the bank within thirty days of receiving
the bank's decision. The Internal Ombudsman shall review the complaint and
issue a recommendation within thirty days of receipt.
chunks.title: Customer Grievance Redressal Framework

chunks.text:
1.3 Regulatory Reporting
Banks shall report the number and value of complaints received, resolved
and pending to the Reserve Bank of India on a quarterly basis. Unresolved
complaints beyond ninety days shall be highlighted separately in the
report.
chunks.title: Customer Grievance Redressal Framework

chunks.text:
1.4 Service Quality Standards
Banks shall ensure that the grievance redressal process does not require
the customer to repeatedly provide the same information. Complaints shall
not be rejected solely on the ground that the customer did not follow a
specific format, provided the complaint contains the essential details.
chunks.title: Customer Grievance Redressal Framework

chunks.text:
1. Applicability
These directions shall apply to all Scheduled Commercial Banks, including
regional rural banks and urban cooperative banks, in respect of their
customer acquisition and account operations. Every bank shall implement a
robust KYC framework covering customer acceptance, customer due diligence,
ongoing monitoring and record keeping.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1.1 Customer Due Diligence
Before opening an account or establishing a business relationship, a bank
shall identify the customer and verify the customer's identity using
reliable and independent sources. For individual customers, verification
shall be based on any one officially valid document such as a passport,
driving licence, Voter ID, Aadhaar card or NREGA job card.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1.2 Risk-Based Approach
Banks shall classify customers into low, medium and high risk categories
based on risk perception. Simplified due diligence shall apply to low risk
customers while enhanced due diligence, including verification of the
source of funds and beneficial ownership, shall apply to high risk
customers and to politically exposed persons.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1.3 Periodic Updation of KYC Records
KYC records of low risk customers shall be updated at least once every ten
years and records of medium and high risk customers shall be updated at
least once every eight years. On failure to update KYC records within the
stipulated period, the bank may restrict the operation of the account.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1.4 Record Retention
Banks shall preserve all records pertaining to the identification of
customers and their account profiles for a period of five years after the
business relationship has ended. Records of transactions shall be preserved
for a minimum of five years from the date of the transaction.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1.5 E-KYC
Banks may carry out electronic KYC using the Aadhaar authentication service
or the DigiLocker facility subject to the consent of the customer and
compliance with the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other
Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.
chunks.title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms

chunks.text:
1. Amendment to Periodic Updation Frequency
This circular amends clause 1.3 of the Master Direction on Know Your
Customer norms issued under Circular No RBI/2025-26/09. With effect from
the date of this circular, KYC records of all customers, irrespective of
risk classification, shall be updated at least once every five years.
chunks.title: Amendment to KYC Master Direction - Periodic Updation

chunks.text:
1.1 Application to Existing Accounts
The revised updation frequency shall apply to all accounts existing on the
date of this circular and to all accounts opened thereafter. Branches shall
complete the updation of all existing accounts within the next updation
cycle.
chunks.title: Amendment to KYC Master Direction - Periodic Updation

chunks.text:
1.2 Consequences of Non-Updation
Where KYC records remain un-updated beyond five years from the last
updation, the bank shall restrict the operation of the account until the
records are updated, and shall communicate the reason to the customer in
writing.
chunks.title: Amendment to KYC Master Direction - Periodic Updation

chunks.text:
1.3 Supersession
To the extent the provisions of clause 1.3 and clause 1.4 of the earlier
master direction are inconsistent with this circular, the provisions of
this circular shall prevail.
chunks.title: Amendment to KYC Master Direction - Periodic Updation
